_comment: huelink configuration. Copy this file to your zigbee2mqtt data directory
(next to configuration.yaml) as 'huelink.config.json' and edit the values.
Every field is optional: a missing file or a missing field falls back to the
default shown here. An INVALID value is not silent, it is reported as an
ERROR in the zigbee2mqtt log with the field name, and that one field falls
The values below ARE the defaults, so this file as shipped changes nothing.
Most pacer fields are re-read while zigbee2mqtt runs: save the file, wait a
couple of seconds, and the log says 'config changed, applied: ...'. Fields
that need a restart say RESTART REQUIRED in their description, and the log
names them too rather than appearing to have taken them.
JSON has no comments, so each field is described in '_fields' below and in
the README. Keys starting with '_' are ignored by the loader.

_fields.device: zigbee2mqtt friendly_name of the gradient strip. This is also the POWER switch: turning this light off stops whatever huelink was doing. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.segments: Number of gradient segments the strip addresses. The Hue Play gradient lightstrip (LCX002) has 7. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.udpPort: UDP port huelink listens on for raw RGB frames. Point your Hyperion 'udpraw' output device at this port on this host. Any free port works as long as both sides agree. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.udpBind: Address the UDP listener binds to. '0.0.0.0' means every interface, which is what a Hyperion running on another machine needs. Set it to '127.0.0.1' when Hyperion runs on this same host, and the port stops existing for the rest of the network. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.udpAllowFrom: List of IP addresses allowed to send frames, for example ['192.168.1.50']. Empty means anyone who can reach the port. A frame carries no sender identity and no password, so whoever reaches the port drives the strip; this is the list that limits that. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.tickMs: How often the loop runs, in milliseconds, 1 to 1000. This is NOT the frame rate: how many frames really go out is the pacer's decision. The loop runs more often than frames go out so that a sudden scene change is noticed immediately. Lowering it to 10 halves the worst-case delay before a cut is noticed, and costs a little CPU; on its own it does not make the strip faster. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.startSettleMs: How long after startup the extension makes no decisions, so that echoes of commands from the previous process can finish arriving. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields._pacing: --- The fields below decide how much of the Zigbee coordinator the strip is allowed to take from the rest of the house. Read docs/PACING.md before raising any of them. ---
_fields.fps: Target frame rate for sync and effects, 1 to 'maxFps'. This is only the STARTING value: Home Assistant and the zigbee2mqtt device page own it afterwards, so editing it here while running is ignored on purpose rather than fighting the slider. Change it from Home Assistant instead. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.maxFps: Highest frame rate the slider and MQTT will accept, 1 to 50. The default of 5 comes from a send cost measured on a coordinator SHARED with the rest of the house. A coordinator dedicated to the strip may carry more: see 'Separate coordinator' in the README before raising this. Raising it does not raise 'fps', it only permits it. RESTART REQUIRED, because the device page builds its slider from this number when zigbee2mqtt loads the converter.
_fields.dutyCap: How many frames may go out in any single 100 ms window, 1 to 10. A hard instantaneous ceiling and therefore an fps ceiling too: 2 per 100 ms is 20 fps, so going above 20 needs 3. This is the number that bounds how many of our frames can ever sit ahead of a wall switch press. Home Assistant owns it afterwards; this is only where it starts. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.occupancyBudget: Fraction of wall clock time (0.05 to 0.9) the stream may keep the Zigbee coordinator busy. This is the one number that protects the rest of the house. The frame rate it can pay for is roughly occupancyBudget divided by the measured frame cost: at the measured 51 ms, 0.35 buys about 6.9 fps. HA shows it as 'HueLink air budget' in percent (5 to 90). This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields._quality: --- Picture quality. These change how the strip looks rather than how much air it uses. Each has a Home Assistant slider that owns the value while running; the file only sets the starting value. ---
_fields.smoothingFactor: Fade time as a multiple of the measured gap between frames, 1 to 2. Above 1 so the colour never comes to rest between frames, which is the stutter this exists to remove. Higher is smoother but leaves the strip further behind the picture. This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.bigChangeThreshold: How many perceptual thresholds a colour change must cross to count as a scene cut, 1 to 40. A cut may skip the frame clock: 1 means every visible change is a cut, 40 is effectively off. This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.fastSmoothingMs: Fade time for a scene cut, 0 to 500 ms. Short on purpose: a cut is the one moment the strip is visibly behind the picture. 20 to 40 is the range worth trying. This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.maxFastPerSec: How many times per second a scene cut may skip the frame clock, 0 to 10. A ration, not a mode: without it a strobe would be 'all cuts' and the fps setting would control nothing. 0 switches the fast path off. The worst case stays fps + maxFastPerSec. This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.saturation: Colour saturation multiplier, 0.5 to 2. 1.0 sends the pixels exactly as the TV sent them. Above 1 pulls colours away from grey (past about 1.7 half-tones collapse into flat primaries); below 1 mutes them. Costs the coordinator nothing. HA shows it as 'HueLink saturation' in percent (50 to 200). This is only the STARTING value: the Home Assistant slider owns it afterwards. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields._presets: --- Presets are not configured here; they are data in extension/huelink-lib/presets.json. Picking one sets fps, occupancyBudget and the quality fields above at once (never dutyCap). 'Normal' equals the defaults in this file. What was last chosen in Home Assistant is kept in huelink.state.json next to this file and wins over these starting values at start. ---
_fields._burst: --- The burst. OFF by default. It spends the budget EARLIER, it does not create any. Read the 'Burst' section of docs/PACING.md first. ---
_fields.burstFps: Frame rate during a burst, 0 to 15, or up to 'maxFps' where that was set higher. 0 is OFF and is the default. A burst starts on a scene cut and raises the frame clock for a moment, paid out of credit that quiet scenes put in the bucket. It does NOT raise 'dutyCap', so the worst-case delay it can add to somebody else's command is unchanged; what it changes is how OFTEN the coordinator is busy. LIVE.
_fields.burstMaxMs: Longest a single burst may last, 0 to 5000 ms. The bucket usually ends it sooner. 0 is the second way to switch bursting off. LIVE.
_fields.burstCreditMs: Size of the bucket in COORDINATOR milliseconds, 0 to 5000. This is the real limiter: a burst may only spend what quiet scenes saved, so the long-term average stays 'occupancyBudget' whatever 'burstFps' is. It also bounds the damage, since a burst can never spend more than this above budget. 0 means nothing can be saved up. LIVE.
_fields.burstRefill: Share of unspent budget that accrues as credit, 0 to 1. 1 saves every millisecond the stream did not use. Lower it to make bursts rarer without making them slower. 0 freezes the bucket. LIVE.
_fields.sourceTtlMs: How long a source still counts as alive after its last frame. When it expires, the strip turns off and waits for frames to come back. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.name: Last part of the MQTT topic: <base_topic>/<name> for the retained state, <base_topic>/<name>/command for commands. Commands are NOT on '/set': zigbee2mqtt's own router claims every '<base_topic>/<something>/set' topic and would look '<name>' up as a Zigbee device it has never heard of. RESTART REQUIRED.
_fields.locale: Language of all human-visible strings: 'en' or 'lv'. See extension/huelink-lib/i18n/. RESTART REQUIRED.
